**Checking who is signed in on load**

`apps/react-vite/src/lib/auth.tsx` sets up auth with `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth`. Its `userFn` is `getUser`, which calls `GET /auth/me` and returns `response.data`. `configureAuth` exports `useUser` (a TanStack Query hook around `getUser`) and `AuthLoader`. `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the app in `AuthLoader`, so the `/auth/me` request runs on first load. I didn't open `provider.tsx`, so I'm assuming it renders its fallback while that request is pending.

The session itself is a cookie. `src/lib/api-client.ts` sets `withCredentials = true` on every request, so the cookie goes out with `/auth/me`. The mock handler for that endpoint is in `src/testing/mocks/handlers/auth.ts`.

If the user is signed in, `useUser().data` holds the user. `ProtectedRoute`, also in `auth.tsx` and used in `src/app/router.tsx`, redirects to `paths.auth.login.getHref(location.pathname)` when `user.data` is empty. That redirect carries `redirectTo`, so the user comes back to the page they wanted.

**What happens on a 401**

The response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` handles every API failure. It first shows an error toast through `useNotifications`, using the server's `message` or the Axios error message. If the status is 401, it then does a hard redirect with `window.location.href = paths.auth.login.getHref(redirectTo)`. Afterwards it rejects the promise, so callers still see the error.

`redirectTo` is built from `new URLSearchParams()`, which is empty. Its `.get('redirectTo')` therefore always returns null, and the code always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. The `searchParams` lookup looks like dead code. It may have been meant to read `window.location.search`.

The 401 handling also applies to the `/auth/me` call itself. A signed-out visitor on any page gets an error toast and a redirect to sign-in, including on public pages that call `useUser`, such as the landing page and the auth layout.
